n Metro stations in a city located along a
circular path. Each pair of stations is connected
by a straight track only. Further, each pair of
nearest stations is connected by blue line,
whereas all remaining pairs of stations are
connected by red line. If the number of red lines
is 99 times the number of blue lines, then the
value of n is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Number of blue lines = Number of sides = n

Number of red lines = number of diagonals $= ^{n}C_{2} – n$

According to question, 

${}^{n}C_{2}-n=99n$

$\Rightarrow \frac{n(n-1)}{2}-n=99n$

$\Rightarrow \frac{n-1}{2}-1=99$

$\Rightarrow n=201$

text:
Let f : R $\to$ R be a function which satisfies

f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) $\forall$ x, y $\in$ R. If f(1) = 2 and

g(n) = $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{(n-1)}f(k)$, n $\in$ N then the value of n, for
which g(n) = 20, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given f(1) = 2 ; 

f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)

When x = y = 1 $\Rightarrow$
f(2) = 2 + 2 = 4

When x = 2, y = 1 $\Rightarrow$ f(3) = 4 + 2 = 6

 g(n) = $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{(n-1)}f(k)$

= f(1) + f(2) +.........+ f(n - 1)

= 2 + 4 + 6 + ......+ 2(n - 1)

= 2 $\times$ $\frac{(n-1)(n)}{2}$

$= n^{2} - n$

 Given g(n) = 20

$\Rightarrow$ $n^{2}– n = 20$

$\Rightarrow$ $n^{2} – n – 20 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ n = 5

text:
Let a, b, c $\in$ R be all non-zero and satisfy

$a^{3} + b^{3} + c^{3} = 2$. If the matrix

A = $⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{lll} a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$

satisfies $A^{T}A = I$, then a value of abc can be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $A$ is symmetric, $A^{T}A=A^{2}=I$. Comparing entries,

$a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1,ab+bc+ca=0.$

Then $(a+b+c)^{2}=1+2(0)=1$, so $a+b+c=\pm 1$, and

$a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}-3abc=(a+b+c)(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}-ab-bc-ca)=\pm 1.$

With $a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}=2$, this gives $2-3abc=\pm 1$, so $abc=\dfrac{1}{3}$ or $abc=1$. Only $\dfrac{1}{3}$ is among the options.

Note: strictly, the given data are inconsistent. $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1$ forces $|a|,|b|,|c|\leq 1$, so $|a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}|\leq |a|^{3}+|b|^{3}+|c|^{3}\leq a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1$, and $a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}=2$ cannot hold for real $a,b,c$. The intended answer, which is also NTA's key, is the one the algebra above gives.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
Let f : (–1,
$\infty$)
$\to$ R be defined by f(0) = 1 and

f(x) = $\frac{1}{x}\log _{e}(1+x)$, x $\neq$ 0. Then the function f :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x\neq 0$,

$f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{\dfrac{x}{1+x}-\ln (1+x)}{x^{2}}=\dfrac{x-(1+x)\ln (1+x)}{x^{2}(1+x)}$

The denominator is positive on $(-1,0)\cup (0,\infty )$, so $f^{'}(x)$ has the sign of $g(x)=x-(1+x)\ln (1+x)$.

$g^{'}(x)=1-\ln (1+x)-1=-\ln (1+x)$

For $-1<x<0$, $\ln (1+x)<0$, so $g^{'}(x)>0$: $g$ increases up to $g(0)=0$, hence $g(x)<0$ on $(-1,0)$.

For $x>0$, $g^{'}(x)<0$: $g$ decreases from $g(0)=0$, hence $g(x)<0$ on $(0,\infty )$.

So $f^{'}(x)<0$ for every $x\neq 0$ in $(-1,\infty )$. Also $\lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{\ln (1+x)}{x}=1=f(0)$, so $f$ is continuous at $0$ and is therefore decreasing on the whole of $(-1,\infty )$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
For some $θ\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$, if the eccentricity of the

hyperbola, $x^{2}–y^{2}\sec ^{2}θ$ = 10 is
$\sqrt{5}$ times the

eccentricity of the ellipse, $x^{2}\sec ^{2}θ$ $+ y^{2} = 5$, then
the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given equation of hyperbola $\Rightarrow x^{2}-y^{2}\sec ^{2}θ=10$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x^{2}}{10}-\frac{y^{2}}{10\cos ^{2}θ}=1$

Hence eccentricity of hyperbola

$(e_{H})=\sqrt{1+\frac{10\cos ^{2}θ}{10}}$   ...(i)

    $\left \{\because e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}}\right \}$

Now equation of ellipse $\Rightarrow x^{2}\sec ^{2}θ+y^{2}=5$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x^{2}}{5\cos ^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{5}=1$   $\left \{e=1-\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}\right \}$

Hence eccenticity of ellipse

$(e_{E})=\sqrt{1-\frac{5\cos ^{2}θ}{5}}$

$(e_{E})=\sqrt{1-\cos ^{2}θ}$   ...(ii)

given $e_{H}=\sqrt{5}e_{e}$

Hence $\sqrt{1+\cos ^{2}θ}=\sqrt{5}\times \left (\sqrt{1-\cos ^{2}θ}\right )$

Squaring both sides

$1+\cos ^{2}θ=5\left (1-\cos ^{2}θ\right )$

$1+\cos ^{2}θ=5-5\cos ^{2}θ$

$6\cos ^{2}θ=4$

$\cos ^{2}θ=\frac{2}{3}$   ...(iii)

Now length of latus rectum of ellipse = $=\frac{2a^{2}}{b}=\frac{10\cos ^{2}θ}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{20}{3\sqrt{5}}=\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{3}$

text:
If a curve y = f(x), passing through the point
(1, 2), is the solution of the differential equation,

$2x^{2}dy= (2xy + y^{2})dx$, then $f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2x^{2}dy=\left (2xy+y^{2}\right )dx$

$\Rightarrow 2x^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}=2xy+y^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{2x^{2}}{2x^{2}y^{2}}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2xy}{2x^{2}y^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{2x^{2}y^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^{2}}\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{1}{x}\frac{1}{y}=\frac{1}{2x^{2}}$

Let $-\frac{1}{y}=t$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^{2}}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dt}{dx}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dt}{dx}+t\frac{1}{x}=\frac{1}{2x^{2}}$

This is linear differentiatial equation.

$\therefore I.F=e^{\int \frac{1}{x}dx}=e^{\ln x}$

$\therefore t.e^{\ln x}=\int \frac{1}{2x^{2}}.e^{\ln x}dx$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{y}.x=\int \frac{1}{2x^{2}}.xdx$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{x}{y}=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{x}$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{x}{y}=\frac{1}{2}\ln x+c$

This curve passes through the point (1, 2)

$\therefore -\frac{1}{2}=0+c$

$\Rightarrow c=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore -\frac{x}{y}=\frac{1}{2}\ln x-\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow -\frac{2x}{y}=\ln x-1$

$\Rightarrow y=\frac{2x}{1-\ln x}$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{2x}{1-\ln x}$

So, $f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\frac{2\times \frac{1}{2}}{1-\ln \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}=\frac{1}{1+\log _{e}2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
If the variance of the terms in an increasing A.P.,
 $b_{1}$
, $b_{2}$
, $b_{3}$
,....,$b_{11}$ is 90, then the common
difference of this $A.P. is_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the common difference = d

and $b_{1}=a$

$b_{2}=a+d$

$b_{3}=a+2d$ 

... $b_{11}=a+10d$

Variance = $\frac{\sum a_{i}^{2}}{11}-\left (\frac{\sum a_{i}}{11}\right )^{2}=90$

$\Rightarrow \frac{a^{2}+(a+d)^{2}+...+(a+10d)^{2}}{11}-\left (\frac{a+(a+d)+...+(a+10d)}{11}\right )^{2}=90$

$\Rightarrow 11\left [11a^{2}+385d^{2}+110ad\right ]-[11a+55d]^{2}=10890$

$\Rightarrow 1210d^{2}=10890$

$\Rightarrow d^{2}=9$

$\Rightarrow d=\pm 3$

As A.P is increasing so d should be positive

$\therefore$ d = 3

text:
If y = $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}k\cos ^{-1}\left \{\frac{3}{5}\cos kx-\frac{4}{5}\sin kx\right \}$,

then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at x = 0 is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put, $\cos α=\frac{3}{5},\sin α=\frac{4}{5}$

$\therefore \frac{3}{5}\cos kx-\frac{4}{5}\sin kx$

$=\cos α.\cos kx-\sin α.\sin kx$

$=\cos (α+kx)$

So, $y=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}k\cos ^{-1}(\cos (α+kx))$

$=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}\left (k^{2}x+kα\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{6}k^{2}$

$=\frac{6\times 7\times 13}{6}=91$

text:
Let [t] denote the greatest integer less than or
equal to t. 
Then the value of $\int\limits _{1}^{2}|2x-[3x]|dx$ is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{1}^{2}|2x-[3x]|dx$ 

$=\int\limits _{1}^{2}|2x-(3x-\{3x\})|dx$

$=\int\limits _{1}^{2}|\{3x\}-x|dx$

We know, 0 $\leq$ $\{3x\}<1$ and x > 1

$\therefore \{3x\}-x<0$

So, $|\{3x\}-2|=-[\{3x\}-x]$

$=\int\limits _{1}^{2}(x-\{3x\})dx$

$=\left [\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right ]_{1}^{2}-\int\limits _{3\times \frac{1}{3}}^{6\times \frac{1}{3}}\{3x\}dx$   [Period of {x} = 1, so period of {3x} = $\frac{1}{3}$]

$=\left (2-\frac{1}{2}\right )-(6-3)\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{3}}3xdx$

$=\frac{3}{2}-3\times 3\left [\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right ]_{0}^{\frac{1}{3}}$

$=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{9}{2}\left [\frac{1}{9}-0\right ]$

$=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2}$ = 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot
